entries.clue: After having gained seat, electoral divisions moving to centre? (7)

blocks.note: A candidate who has won a seat is IN, elected.
Wards are the divisions a council area is split into for voting.

annotation.surface: A party that has just won a seat shuffles its constituency boundaries towards the political centre.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'centre' politically, as a party drifting to the middle ground; the definition means it literally, heading towards the middle of something.
annotation.definitionFit: Something moving inwards travels from the outside towards the middle, and the question mark flags the political sense the surface pushes.

entries.clue: LibDems no longer try paid HRT treatment (5,5)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition is a description rather than a synonym: the Liberal Democrats are what the answer no longer names, having lost third place in the Commons.

indicatorNotes.treatment: Treatment works something over and changes its state, so the letters beside it are processed into a new order.

blocks.note: These ten letters are rearranged.

annotation.surface: The Liberal Democrats have stopped trying to get hormone replacement therapy paid for.
annotation.walkthrough: HRT is hormone replacement therapy, so 'treatment' sits naturally beside it in the surface. After the 2015 election the SNP overtook the Liberal Democrats in seats, taking third place in the Commons.
annotation.definitionFit: A third party is the third-largest in a parliament, the role the Liberal Democrats held in the Commons until the SNP took it in 2015.

entries.clue: Chamber gets dirt on Blair, his right wing having deserted (6)

indicatorNotes.on: In a down entry the piece written on another sits above it, so the first piece comes before the second.

blocks.note: Grot is British slang for dirt or rubbish.
Tony Blair, the former Labour prime minister.
The right-hand half of TONY is removed.

annotation.surface: Someone digs up dirt on Tony Blair now that his right-wing supporters have abandoned him.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Right wing' reads as Blair's centrist New Labour allies, but it means the right-hand end of his first name. Removing it leaves the first half.
annotation.definitionFit: A grotto is a cave or cavern, a natural chamber in rock.

entries.clue: Standard celebs full of 'beach bollocks' (5,3,7)

indicatorNotes.full of: Something full of other things holds them inside it, so the next pieces go inside the first.

blocks.note: Celebrities are stars.
A beach is the sands.
Tripe is rubbish or nonsense, which is what 'bollocks' means here.

annotation.surface: Celebrities are being accused of spouting nonsense about the beach.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Standard' looks like a measure or a norm, but it is a flag. SANDS and TRIPE go in together, filling STARS between its last two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag or banner, and the Stars and Stripes is the flag of the United States.

entries.clue: Left only falling apart – indeed so (3-5)

indicatorNotes.falling apart: Something falling apart loses its shape, so the letters that follow come loose and rearrange.

blocks.note: These eight letters are rearranged.

annotation.surface: Someone agrees that the political left is collapsing, with only a dash and 'indeed so'.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Indeed so' reads as a speaker's agreement tacked on after the dash, but it supplies the letters. 'Left only' is the definition: seeing things from the left alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A view that takes in only the left, and nothing from the right, is one-sided: partial and biased.

entries.clue: Far right of Trump? In favour of uprising? That's academic (4)

indicatorNotes.Far right of: The far right of a word is its rightmost letter, where the word ends.
indicatorNotes.uprising: In a down entry a word that rises is read from bottom to top, so it runs backwards.

blocks.note: The last letter of TRUMP.
In favour of is FOR, reversed.

annotation.surface: A commentator asks whether Trump's far-right supporters would back a revolt, and dismisses the question as academic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Far right' and 'uprising' pull towards politics, but one points at the end of a name and the other turns a word upside down. 'That's academic' reads as 'that's beside the point'; the definition is the person.
annotation.definitionFit: Prof is the short form of professor, the senior academic in a university department.

entries.clue: Inappropriate nursery worker's show of affection (7)

blocks.note: A nursery worker who hits the children is one who smacks, something no nursery allows.
A loud kiss on the lips is British slang for the same word.

annotation.surface: A nursery worker is disciplined for showing the children too much affection.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a worker who is too affectionate, but the first reading is a worker who smacks the children. The second is informal British English for a loud kiss.
annotation.definitionFit: A smacker is someone who smacks, which is wrong in a nursery, and also a slang word for a noisy kiss.

entries.clue: Support from Cameron: "without me, awful hot inside" (6)

indicatorNotes.without: Without means lacking, so the named letters are taken away.
indicatorNotes.awful: Something awful is in a bad state, so the letters are thrown out of order.
indicatorNotes.inside: Inside puts the named letter in among the others before they are rearranged.

blocks.note: The name is taken as letters.
These two letters are taken out of the name, leaving CARON.
H for hot, as on a tap.

annotation.surface: David Cameron hints that his party will manage badly without him, a heated row going on behind closed doors.
annotation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it sound like a speech by Cameron, but his surname is just the raw letters. Only once ME is out and H is in do the six letters get rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: An anchor is something that holds a thing steady and keeps it in place, so it is a figurative support.

entries.clue: Outbursts from unsmart 'deplorable' following Trump's lead (8)

indicatorNotes.deplorable: Something deplorable is in a wretched state, so the letters beside it are scrambled.
indicatorNotes.following: In an across entry a piece following another comes after it, so the first letter goes in front.
indicatorNotes.lead: A word's lead is the letter that goes first.

blocks.note: The first letter of TRUMP.
These seven letters are rearranged.

annotation.surface: The less clever members of Hillary Clinton's 'basket of deplorables' copy their candidate's outbursts.
annotation.walkthrough: In 2016 Hillary Clinton called half of Trump's supporters 'a basket of deplorables', so the word looks like a label for his fans. Here it only scrambles 'unsmart'.
annotation.definitionFit: Tantrums are fits of childish rage, and outbursts is a plain synonym for them.

entries.clue: Duty is making a comeback: which Trump needs to be open about (3,7)

annotation.definition: which Trump needs to be open about
annotation.definitionNote: The relative clause stands for the thing it describes, so it takes the place of a noun phrase.

blocks.note: A duty is a tax, as on imported goods.
Something that is making a comeback returns.

annotation.surface: Pressure on Trump returns over something he ought to disclose.
annotation.walkthrough: In the 2016 campaign Trump broke with custom by refusing to publish his tax returns. 'Returns' is a verb in the wordplay and a noun, the filed forms, in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Tax returns are the forms filed with the tax authorities, which US presidential candidates had customarily published and Trump would not release.

entries.clue: (& 22ac.) Dial Bill, Hillary's "chief source of energy" and misery guts (4)

indicatorNotes.chief: The chief of something is its head, so the word gives its first letter.
indicatorNotes.source: A source is where something starts, so the word gives its first letter.

blocks.note: The dial of a clock is its face.
AC, short for account, is a bill.
The first letter of HILLARY.
The first letter of ENERGY.

annotation.surface: Bill Clinton, whom Hillary calls her chief source of energy, turns out to be a grump.
annotation.walkthrough: Bill and Hillary look like the Clintons but supply only an account and a letter. Face-ache is British slang for a sour, gloomy person.
annotation.definitionFit: Face-ache is British slang for a miserable-looking person, and misery guts is another British name for the same habitual moaner.

entries.clue: Ambassadorial jerk dropped certificate (7)

indicatorNotes.dropped: Something dropped is let go, so the named letters are left out of the longer word.

blocks.note: Ambassadors are diplomats, so ambassadorial work is diplomatic.
A tic is a sudden involuntary jerk; these letters are removed from the end.

annotation.surface: An idiot of an ambassador has been stripped of his credentials.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' looks like an insult for the ambassador but is a twitch. Taking the twitch off the end of the adjective leaves the award.
annotation.definitionFit: A diploma is a certificate awarded for finishing a course of study.

entries.clue: Bum duke, wanker, gets time off (6)

indicatorNotes.off: Something taken off is removed, so the named letter goes.

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for duke.
Tosser is a British insult meaning the same as wanker.
T for time, removed from the front of TOSSER.

annotation.surface: A worthless aristocrat, insulted as a wanker, is given time off work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bum' reads as a backside or a rude adjective for the duke, but it is a noun for a vagrant. 'Dosser' is British slang for someone who sleeps rough.
annotation.definitionFit: A dosser is British slang for a homeless person who sleeps rough, and a bum is the American word for the same down-and-out.

entries.clue: Go off sex rotten, as drunks usually do (5,2,3)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition is a descriptive clause standing for the action itself, so it replaces a verb phrase.

blocks.note: To go off is to drop off to sleep.
IT is old slang for sex, or sex appeal.
Food that has gone rotten is off.

annotation.surface: Drunks are known to go off sex, finding it rotten.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Go off' reads as losing interest in sex, but it means falling asleep. 'It' for sex is a crossword standard, from phrases like 'doing it'.
annotation.definitionFit: To sleep it off is to recover from being drunk by sleeping until the effects wear off, which is how most drunks end the night.

entries.clue: Clinton's blueprint scheme put before Republican? (5,6)

annotation.definitionNote: Clinton is an example of the answer, as the question mark signals, and the apostrophe-s reads as 'is', joining name to wordplay.

indicatorNotes.put before: Put before places one piece ahead of the next, so the scheme comes in front of the final letter.

blocks.note: A blueprint is a draft, a first plan.
A dodge is a crafty scheme.
R is the standard abbreviation for Republican.

annotation.surface: Hillary Clinton's plan is set against the Republican candidate's.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about Hillary's policy plan against Trump, but it is Bill Clinton, who avoided the Vietnam War draft as a young man.
annotation.definitionFit: A draft dodger avoids being conscripted, and Bill Clinton was accused of it over the Vietnam draft, so he is an example.

entries.clue: France used Iran fee to provide sumptuous spread? (4,4)

indicatorNotes.used: Something used is worn and knocked about, no longer in its original shape, so the letters are rearranged.

blocks.note: F is the international code for France.
These seven letters join the F to be rearranged.

annotation.surface: France spends money received from Iran on a lavish banquet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Used' looks like France spending the fee, but it is what rearranges the letters. Fine Fare was also a British supermarket chain, which accounts for the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: Fine fare is excellent food, which is what a sumptuous spread offers; the question mark points to the old supermarket name as well.

entries.clue: Blunders, accepting extremely Conservative means of relaxing arms (7)

indicatorNotes.accepting: Something that accepts another takes it in, so one piece goes inside the other.
indicatorNotes.extremely: The extremes of a word are its two ends, so the first and last letters are taken.

blocks.note: To blunder is to trip up, so blunders is TRIPS.
The first and last letters of CONSERVATIVE.

annotation.surface: Mistakes by the Conservatives are blamed on relaxing arms controls.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Relaxing arms' sounds like easing weapons controls, but it is the body's arms. The biceps bend the elbow and the triceps straighten it again.
annotation.definitionFit: The triceps is the muscle at the back of the upper arm that straightens the elbow, undoing the bend.

entries.clue: Suspend Jordan's bust with uranium implant (7)

indicatorNotes.bust: Something bust is broken, so the letters are rearranged.
indicatorNotes.implant: An implant is something put inside, so the letter goes into the others.

blocks.note: The name is taken as letters.
U is the chemical symbol for uranium.

annotation.walkthrough: Jordan was the stage name of Katie Price, a British glamour model known for breast implants, so 'bust' and 'implant' read as her figure. Both are instructions.

entries.clue: May's political persuasion needs injection of flash colour (6)

indicatorNotes.needs injection of: An injection puts something into a body, so the second piece goes inside the first.

blocks.note: Theresa May is a Conservative, shortened to CON.
A flash of light is a ray.

annotation.walkthrough: 'Colour' looks like a noun for a hue, but it is a verb, and the answer is a verb too. Theresa May was prime minister when this was set in 2016.
annotation.definitionFit: Crayon works as a verb as well as a noun: drawing over a picture with coloured wax sticks fills it with colour, the way a child colours in a book.

entries.clue: (& 25ac.) Bogus accusation from contender: "Hislop raised fee!" (7)

blocks.note: Donald Trump was a presidential contender in 2016.
Ian Hislop is the editor of Private Eye, where this crossword appears.
Something raised is up.
A fee is a charge.

annotation.walkthrough: 'Hislop' is Private Eye's editor, so the magazine's own crossword uses him for ED. Trump was a contender for the presidency when this appeared in October 2016.

entries.clue: Recovery of "rehabilitated" Trump accepted by international body? Miles off! (6)

indicatorNotes.rehabilitated: To rehabilitate is to reform and restore, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order.
indicatorNotes.accepted by: Something accepted by another is taken into it, so these letters go inside the outer piece.

entries.clue: "Sexual overtures" trial? Not if quashed (10)

"To be a better  person is about being supportive" – May's opener (6)
